cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: Early players appreciate the modernized graphics, remastered music, and vast array of campaigns and civilizations.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features updated graphics, remastered soundtracks, and an extensive selection of campaigns and civilizations.

citations.review_text:
This is still the ultimate RTS stuffed with endless campaigns and countless civilizations to make offline and online play (Casual and Competitive) stay fresh even after hundreds of hours.
The updated graphics of this definitive edition keeps the game up to date for modern times and the remastered soundtrack is just as memorable as the originals.
They've also added even more difficulty modes to most of the campaigns ensuring a good experience even if you are not the most skilled AoE 2 player.
The modding scene is also as vibrant as ever if you somehow think there still isn't enough content with many great custom campaigns for single player and modes for multiplayer.
Whether it's against AI, each other or doing co-op through the campaigns, you can't do better than this classic remastered RTS.

For me this is the best RTS ever made. It has a tight set of simple rules that are easy to get into and hard to master. A fun gameplay loop, that is always prompting another game with it's short play times. Perfect for multiplayer. With a huge variety cultures you can play as, that have been added over the years with loads of cool DLC, each slightly changes the overall play style to keep the game feeling new. The fact that the game is still supported over all these years tells you everything you need to know. Well worth the money for just simple fun-factor. Oh, and the improved "classic" graphics make it look super 90's cool. 
I love this game.

single_points.text: One reviewer says the AI constantly rushes the player and can outpace them at every step.

citation.review_text:
I am reviewing this from a strictly single player perspective, please keep that in mind.
That being said, I do not recommend this game for someone seeking a good single player RTS.
- The AI can outpace that player at every step of the way.
The first few missions in the first starter campaign are fine, but as soon as you step out of that one the AI is suddenly that same thing 90% of RTS are that focus more on single player. 
- "Rush the player" constantly is such an over used tactic for weak AI. You can't sit back and enjoy getting your civilization up and running because the enemy AI just keeps attacking, attacking, attacking and soon you find yourself spending 80% of your time defending yourself, repairing damage then trying to get back to setting up a farm.  I don't see how this is enjoyable from a single player perspective.
- Even if you focus on defense from the start, you are still running against the clock of "how soon will the enemy send an annoying force that I have to prepare for.
- I get this a "war" based game, but when a human being has to jungle 30 different things at once when the AI can do the same thing in 0.5 seconds it because a game of frustration rather than strategy or tactics.
- The only tactic that works at is to focus purely on military and quickly overwhelm the enemy with a massive force. How is that "strategy" when it's just "how fast can you click".

I know I'm going to be the odd man out on my review, and that's fine, but there are some of us who love the setting and the idea of bringing up your civilization AND having military conflict, but this game seems to only care about the military part and all the other stuff is just window dressing.

And before someone yells at me "this game is for multiplayer, yeah I get that, but it is sold and listened as single player as well, why bother with single player campaigns then?

Functionally the game runs great, looks good and is pretty bug free, gameplay wise, it's just not enjoyable.

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Mid-tier players enjoy the deep strategic gameplay and consistent historical depth.

single_points.text: One reviewer says that getting all the faction adding DLCs so that you have everything at your disposal for ranked play is a fairly expensive endeavor.

citation.review_text:
I am FAR away from being the most knowledgeable person when it come to this series but I do earnestly think this is a very, VERY fun traditional base building rts game.

While I have yet to play a PVP match or any of the campaigns, I have gotten over 30 hours of playtime from "skirmish" and "comp stomp" matches alone in a little over 2 weeks.
Things I particularly like about AoE2DE at the moment include the way the game structures its factions, the soundtrack of the game and some specific factions I have grown to like (Namely The Sicilians and Hindustanis).

On the other hand, things I dislike about the game largely include things that can be chalked up to skill-issues(Feeling stressed from having a bunch of enemies in your base, having your invasion force killed off easily, etc). I will also note that -> from what I've seen <-, getting all the faction adding DLCs so that you have everything at your disposal for ranked play is a fairly expensive endeavor.

In conclusion, I really like this game and I will try to remember to update my review of it after I get some hands on experience with the PVP (Maybe including some ranked 1v1's) and campaigns of this game.

single_points.text: One reviewer says the online mode against other players is wonky and you have to deal with hiccups and bugs.

citation.review_text: Will preface by saying the online mode against other players is wonky, unless you can deal with hiccups and bugs then I wouldn't recommend this game for this reason. What I can recommend it for is it's campaign and especially playing with friends vs an AI. Yes, this might sound like it's unfair but unless you really know what you are doing, it's gonna be tough as you increase the difficulty of the AI. A classic RTS that has to be experienced, give it a shot.

cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Longtime players continue to enjoy the deep mechanics despite occasional frustration with unit movement.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that unit pathfinding remains suboptimal in the definitive edition.

citations.review_text: AGE old classic, much better graphics. Gameplay highly improved, unit pathfinding etc. Honestly dlc is what we were looking for. more diverse Civs and playing with teams make some pretty good combos. Updates bi-monthly(at least ive noticed).

all time classic with a competitive scene stronger than ever
lovely community, regular updates, DLCs, balancing fixes

pathing still suboptimal :)

wololo

9/10 imo
 
pathfinding could improve, all else great

single_points.text: One reviewer says there is anti-cheat in the single-player campaign.

citation.review_text:
I play this game for the campaign and ever since what ever stupid company took over the remake and updates it has been VEEERRRYYYY consistently like trying to enjoy CBT. When i played the original demo, you played the William Wallace campaign tutorial thing and you could advance to the imperial age as the Celts with 200 pop cap. Every new campaign is like "You are limited to 50 units and are versing 7 enemies  who are in imperial age. They have every siege unit but you are limited to militia and the dark ages and if you lose this non-functioning building, you lose. You have 10 minutes to kill 5 enemies and they will rebuild buildings instantly after they are destroyed. They have unlimited resources btw." Only a slight exaggeration. 

I used to just muddle thru it using WAND to at least maybe enjoy it a bit more but they have ANTI CHEAT in the campaign. Single Player Campaign. The only thing I was enjoying about this game was getting the campaign achievements and I cant even do that anymore. If I could refund, I would in a heart beat. This game is aimed solely at the "Pros" and I don't care about it anymore. Back to Starcraft 2 I go potentially forever or at least until that shuts down.
